He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara Gauchos]]. ==Early life and education== Nunnally was born in [[San Jose, California]],{{cite web |title=James Nunnally - 2011-12 - Men's Basketball |url=https://ucsbgauchos.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/james-nunnally/434 |website=University of California, Santa Barbara |access-date=February 4, 2025}} and attended [[Weston Ranch High School]] in [[Stockton, California]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 10 points and 8.4 rebounds per game. As a junior, he averaged 19 points, 6.5 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game as he was named Stockton Record Player of the Year, All-State, All-CIF Sac-Joaquin Section and All-Valley Oak League.{{cite web | url=http://ucsbgauchos.com/sports/m-baskbl/2011-12/bios/nunnally%20james00.html | title=21 – James Nunnally | work=ucsbgauchos.com | access-date=July 8, 2014}} In November 2007, Nunnally signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play [[college basketball]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].{{cite news|title=UCSB Lands Loyola Marymount Transfer Orlando Johnson|url=http://ucsb.prestosports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/060608aaa.html|access-date=July 8, 2014|work=PrestoSports.com|date=June 6, 2008}} As a senior, he averaged 22.1 points, 8.3 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 1.9 steals, and 1.2 blocks per game as he helped Weston Ranch to a perfect 14–0 record in the Valley Oak League. He was named All-State, Valley Oak League Most Valuable Player, All-CIF Sac-Joaquin Section, first-team All-Valley Oak League, and Stockton Record Player of the Year. He was a McDonald's All-American nominee. In his freshman season at [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara]], Nunnally was one of four Gauchos to play in all 31 games, starting seven midway through the season. In those 31 games, he averaged 7.9 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/james-nunnally-1.html |title=James Nunnally Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=July 8, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140330064927/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/james-nunnally-1.html |archive-date=March 30, 2014 }} In his sophomore season, he was a second-team All-Big West choice and a Big West All-Tournament team selection. In 29 games, he averaged 14.7 points, 5.6 rebounds and 1.9 assists in 29.9 minutes per game. In his junior season, he was an Honorable Mention All-Big West choice and was selected to the All-Big West Tournament team after helping the Gauchos to their second straight title. In 32 games, he averaged 16.3 points, 5.7 rebounds and 1.8 assists in 33.0 minutes per game. In his senior season, he was a second-team All-Big West choice for the second time in his career. He was also named to the All-Big West Tournament team for the third straight year. In 31 games, he averaged 16.0 points, 5.9 rebounds and 2.8 assists in 33.7 minutes per game. ==Career== ===2012–13 season=== After failing to be drafted in the [[2012 NBA draft]], Nunnally joined the [[Sacramento Kings]] for the [[2012 NBA Summer League]]. On August 19, 2012, he signed a one-year deal with [[Kavala B.C.|Kavala]] of Greece's [[Greek Basket League|Basket League]].{{cite news|title=Kavala signs Will Coleman and rookie James Nunnally|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/94650/kavala-signs-will-coleman-and-rookie-james-nunnally.html|access-date=July 8, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=August 19, 2012}} In October 2012, he left Kavala, after just three games. On November 2, 2012, he was selected in the second round of the 2012 NBA D-League draft, by the [[Bakersfield Jam]].{{cite news|title=Bakersfield Jam Select Seven Players in 2012 Felice Scandone|Sidigas Avellino]] of Italy for the [[2015–16 Lega Basket Serie A|2015–16 season]].{{cite news|title=Sidigas Avellino announces James Nunnally|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/173548/sidigas-avellino-announces-james-nunnally.html|access-date=August 22, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=August 22, 2015}} He led the club to a 26–14 record and averaged 18.4 points (third highest scorer in the competition), 4.2 rebounds, and 2.5 assists while shooting 90.8% from the free throw line (tops in the league) over those 40 games.{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/league/6/Italian-Lega-Basket-Serie-A/stats/2016/Averages/Qualified/All/points/All/desc/1/Regular_Season|title=Italian Lega Basket Serie A Stats - RealGM|website=basketball.realgm.com}}{{Cite web|url=http://web.legabasket.it/player/NUN-JAM-90/|title=LEGABASKET SERIE A LEGABASKET SERIE A|website=web.legabasket.it}} He subsequently earned [[Lega Basket Serie A MVP|Italian league MVP]] honors.{{cite news|title=M.V.P. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] of Turkey for the [[2016–17 Turkish Basketball Super League|2016–17 season]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/207893/fenerbahce-signs-james-nunnally.html|title=Fenerbahce signs James Nunnally|work=Sportando.com|date=July 28, 2016|access-date=July 28, 2016}}{{cite web|url=http://fenerbahce.org/detay.asp?ContentID=51487|title=JAMES NUNNALLY VE AHMET DÜVERİOĞLU FENERBAHÇE'DE|work=fenerbahce.org|date=July 28, 2016|access-date=July 28, 2016|language=tr}}{{dead link|date=March 2020|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} In the [[2017–18 EuroLeague]] season, Fenerbahçe made it to the [[2018 EuroLeague Final Four]], its fourth consecutive [[EuroLeague Final Four|Final Four]] appearance. |date=June 27, 2021}} ===Partizan (2022–2024)=== In the summer of 2022, Nunnally signed a contract with the Serbian team [[KK Partizan|Partizan]]. During the 2022–23 season, Partizan was eliminated from the [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in a tight [[2023 EuroLeague Playoffs|playoffs]] series. Over the season, Nunnally averaged 9.2 points and 2.1 rebounds per game. Partizan ended the 2022–23 season by lifting the [[2022–23 ABA League First Division|ABA League]] championship trophy, after a 3–2 score against Crvena Zvezda in the Finals series.{{cite news |title=PARTIZAN MOZZART BET ARE 2022/23 ADMIRALBET ABA LEAGUE CHAMPIONS |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news/49109/partizan-mozzart-bet-are-2022-23-admiralbet-aba-league-champions/ |access-date=June 23, 2023 |work=aba-liga.com |date=June 22, 2023}} Over the 2023–24 season, he averaged 12.3 points, 3.2 rebounds and 2.6 assists over 32 EuroLeague games. The season was deemed unsuccessful for Partizan as they finished the season without lifting any trophy.{{cite news |title=Očekuje nas burno leto u Partizanu – ko ostaje, a ko odlazi? |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/srpska-kosarka/28999/ocekuje-nas-burno-leto-u-partizanu-ko-ostaje-a-ko-odlazi/vest |access-date=June 11, 2024 |date=June 6, 2024 |language=Serbian}} ===Zhejiang Lions (2025)=== In January 2025, Nunnally signed with [[Zhejiang Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web |title=Eski Fenerbahçeli, Çin Ligi'nde Boban Marjanovic'in Takım Arkadaşı Oldu! |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/tr/others-tr/1772703/eski-fenerbahceli-cin-liginde-boban-marjanovicin-takim-arkadasi-oldu/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=February 4, 2025 |date=January 17, 2025}} ===AEK Athens (2026)=== On January 1, 2026, Nunnally joined [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL) and the [[Basketball Champions League|FIBA Champions League]].{{Cite web |title=James Nunnally returns to Europe, joins Greek club |url=https://basketnews.com/news-237866-james-nunnally-signs-with-aek-athens.html |access-date=2026-04-03 |website=basketnews.com |language=en}} ==Personal life== Nunnally is the son of Deanna Johnson. Married to wife, Jen, the two recently celebrated their marriage with a vow renewal.
